issues.legal_issue: A pleading amendment adding a relief should be allowed when it does not change the suit’s nature, deprive the opposing party of an accrued limitation right, or cause serious injustice that cannot be compensated by costs.
material_facts: The plaintiff sought to amend the plaint to add a relief for recovery of possession.
The District Judge found that the amendment would cause no grave or serious prejudice to the defendant.
The amendment did not alter the nature of the suit or take away a valuable limitation right accrued to the defendant.
Any prejudice to the defendant could be compensated by costs.
issues.conclusion: The amendment was properly allowed, subject to the plaintiff paying costs and filing the amended plaint as directed; the District Judge’s order was restored.
issues.legal_principle: Under Pirgonda Hongonda Patil v. Kalgonda Shilgonda Patil (1957 SCR 595), the test for allowing an amendment is whether it causes serious injustice to the other side. Courts should be extremely liberal in allowing pleading amendments unless serious injustice or irreparable loss would result; prejudice that can be compensated by costs does not require refusal.

rule.if: civil_suit_amendment and proposed_change_adds_possession_relief and suit_nature_unchanged and no_limitation_right_lost and serious_prejudice_absent and prejudice_compensable_by_costs

predicates.civil_suit_amendment: A party in a civil suit requested an amendment to a pleading.
predicates.proposed_change_adds_possession_relief: The requested change added a claim for recovery of possession.
predicates.suit_nature_unchanged: The requested change did not alter the nature of the suit.
predicates.no_limitation_right_lost: The requested change did not remove a valuable limitation right already accrued to the opposing party.
predicates.serious_prejudice_absent: The amendment would not cause grave or serious prejudice to the opposing party.
predicates.prejudice_compensable_by_costs: Any prejudice to the opposing party could be compensated by an award of costs.

issues.definition: When a civil-suit amendment adds a possession claim without changing the suit’s nature or removing an accrued limitation right, and causes no serious prejudice or only prejudice compensable by costs, the amendment is allowed subject to appropriate conditions.

issues.legal_issue: A revisional court should not set aside a discretionary order allowing a pleading amendment without cogent reasons or compelling circumstances.
material_facts: The District Judge exercised discretion to allow the amendment and found that it would cause no grave or serious prejudice.
The High Court set aside that discretionary order in revision.
The Supreme Court found no cogent reason or compelling circumstance justifying the High Court’s interference.
issues.conclusion: The High Court erred in interfering in revision, and its judgment was set aside while the District Judge’s order was restored.
issues.legal_principle: A revisional court ought not lightly interfere with discretion exercised in allowing an amendment in the absence of cogent reasons or compelling circumstances.

predicates.revision_against_discretionary_amendment: A revision challenged a lower court’s discretionary order allowing a pleading amendment.
predicates.lower_court_exercised_sound_discretion: The lower court exercised its discretion soundly in allowing the amendment.
predicates.no_cogent_reason_for_interference: No cogent reason supported setting aside the lower court’s order.
predicates.no_compelling_circumstance_for_interfere: No compelling circumstance justified setting aside the lower court’s order.

issues.definition: When a revision challenges a sound discretionary order allowing a pleading amendment and there is neither a cogent reason nor a compelling circumstance for setting it aside, revisional interference is unwarranted.
